questions.prompt: To turn the error code of the last failed call into text, use `strerror({{0}})`.
questions.explain: `errno` (from `<errno.h>`) holds the code of the last failure; `strerror` (from `<string.h>`) returns a message such as "No such file or directory".
Errors go to stderr (descriptor 2) so they stay visible when stdout is redirected to a file or a pipe.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (The reason of a failed fopen.)
questions.explain: `fopen` returns NULL and sets `errno` to `ENOENT`; `strerror` gives its message.
The second `mkdir` fails with `EEXIST`, whose message is `File exists`.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (An out-of-range number.)
questions.explain: The value does not fit in a `long`, so `strtol` returns `LONG_MAX` and sets `errno` to `ERANGE`. Set `errno = 0` first so you can tell.
`perror(prefix)` writes `prefix: message` and a newline to stderr, using `errno`. Call it right after the failing call.
options: `open: ` followed by the message of the current errno, on standard error
option_notes: It prints text, not the number.

questions.prompt: When is the value of `errno` meaningful?
questions.explain: Library functions never reset `errno` to 0 on success. Test the return value first, then read `errno`.
options: Right after a call that reported failure; a successful call may leave an old value
Always: it is 0 when everything is fine
option_notes: It is not cleared on success.
Library functions use it as well.
It is read while the program runs.

questions.prompt: What exit status means that a program finished successfully?
questions.explain: By convention 0 is success and any other value signals an error. The shell shows the status of the last command in `$?`.

questions.prompt: Which statements about standard error are true?
questions.explain: Error messages go to stderr so that they stay visible when the normal output is redirected. `perror` also uses stderr, and `errno` is only set on failures.
options: `fprintf(stderr, ...)` is not affected by a redirection like `> out.txt`
`errno` is set to a non-zero value whenever a call succeeds

questions.prompt: To use `errno` you must include the header <{{0}}.h>.
questions.explain: `<errno.h>` declares `errno` and the constants such as `ENOENT` and `EEXIST`.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of handling a failing library call in order.
questions.explain: Check right away, report the reason where it can be seen, and do not continue with a broken state.
items: Compare the return value with the failure value (NULL or -1)
Print a message with strerror(errno) on stderr

questions.prompt: Why are error messages printed to stderr and not to stdout?
questions.explain: A user who runs `prog > result.txt` still sees the errors on the screen, and a program that reads the output does not receive them as data.
options: They stay visible when stdout is redirected to a file or a pipe, and they are not mixed into the program's results
It is required by the compiler
